Nicolette Kinnear [6193]

By: Marion Edmunds | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We meet a police widow fighting for justice after her husband’s murder

Unique Selling Point:
Nicolette Kinnear lost her husband in a cold-blooded assassination in broad daylight on their doorstep, in gang-ridden Bishop Lavis in Cape Town. Lieutenant-Colonel Charl Kinnear was an experienced and award-winning detective who through his investigations disrupted the complex patterns of gang warfare, criminality and police complicity which mark the Cape Flats out as a ganglands. Kinnear’s murder was linked by the police to the crime empire of Nafiz Modack and one of his henchmen, Zane Killian, who had been illegally tracking Kinnear’s movements – apparently 2116 times through cellphone triangulation, depicting his exact movements. At the time of the murder, Kinnear was investigating a gun-running case which implicated Modack and 8 senior policemen. However, there is also speculation that the murder could have been a commissioned gang hit, because of his Kinnear’s success at convicting two 28 members that week. What is clear is that the ongoing vendettas between power blocs within the Western Cape Police Service, and the lack of support Kinnear received from his employer, the SAPS, left the capable and competent detective extremely vulnerable, all the more so after he had fingered officials and exposed faultlines in a whistle-blower’s report two years earlier. Since Kinnear’s death on the 18 September 2020, Nicolette and her two sons have been waiting for justice to be done – and when she got sight of the final IPID report into her husband’s death wanted to speak out about how he and her family have been failed.

Summary:
The court case of Nafiz Modack loaded with extortion charges will take place in September and will include the Charl Kinnear assassination and as well as the attempted murder of Advocate William Booth on 9 April 2020, among many other charges. There will be about 28 accused. Modack is alleged to have funded these particular hits as well as others. This mega-trial will lay bare the story of the “Nafiz Modack Enterprise” which among other things channelled cash to hitmen through his business Empire Investment Cars. As the state lays down the full evidence, so will emerge a portrait of Modack as a violent criminal on the make, heavily involved in racketeering and extortion, with blood on his hands.

Nicolette has been cold-shouldered by the bosses of her husband – former top cops Jeremy Veary and Peter Jacobs, who have made no attempt to reach out to her in this time of desolation.

However, she did receive a letter concealed in a bunch of flower son her husband’s grave which drew a picture of a roundtable discussion involving gang members and police officials which determined her husband’s death. These point the finger at Ralph Stanfield, leader of the 28’s who “own” Bishop Lavis and Valhalla Park. This allegation has not been proved in any way.


Further information:
The convictions secured by Charl Kinnear in the week of his murder were for two 28 gangsters, Ashwin Willemse alias ‘Krag” and Waylin Abdulla alias “Wena” who were found guilty on two counts of murder, aggravated robbery and possession of firearms and ammunition. Their victims were Gregory “Kallie” Carelse who sustained 16 shots to his body, and Prezano Holland on 18 October 2018. Carelse, a local hero in the community, was close to Kinnear as he was a former police reservist. Carelse himself had been involved in arresting members of the Stanfield clan a year earlier, and witness to a drive-by shooting which claimed three lives. Another policeman Colonel Andre Kay who lived a few doors down from the Kinnears was also hit on 14 Nov 2019 outside his residence. His body, pumped with ten bullets, was found by his 81-year old mother in the driveway. He was attached to the Fire Arms, Liquor and Second hand goods Control unit, loved his job, lived with his mother and was universally liked.

Nicolette wants to speak out because she feels the state is failing her family, failed her husband while he was working as an organized crime investigator, and fails other families in her position. Given the rate of murder of community leaders, lawyers and policemen in the Western Cape, her story has relevance.

She takes a deep interest in the trial of Modack, and receives a great deal of inside information from all over, including police reports before they have been tabled. However she is anxious about her safety and her future.

The most recent IPID report, which left her reeling, ought to be tabled in Parliament by controversial ANC politician, Tina Joemat-Pettersen, chair of the police portfolio committee, but there is no clarity when and whether MPs will be using it to hold the failed police service to account.

Many of the people fingered in the IPID report have already left the service, without experiencing any penalties, despite their complicity or neglect. Others who were fingered remain in place in SAPS.

Press Release:


The Ultimate Price
A thorn in the side of organised crime and a spear in the fight for justice, Lieutenant-Colonel Charl Kinnear was a highly decorated detective. His investigations disrupted the complex patterns of gang warfare and police complicity on the Cape Flats, in the Western Cape. It was a dangerous job at the best of times, and Kinnear should’ve enjoyed the support of his commanding officers, but according to an explosive new report, he was abandoned by his police bosses at the height of his investigations. Kinnear paid the ultimate price. After weeks of being tracked and followed by unknown assailants, the Lieutenant-Colonel was gunned down on his own doorstep. Now his wife, Nicolette, has stepped forward demanding justice for her husband’s senseless killing.
Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


(VO)
WHATEVER THE WEATHER, NICOLETTE KINNEAR LAYS FLOWERS ON HER HUSBAND’S GRAVE WEEKLY. IT’S BECOME ROUTINE OVER THE TWENTY-TWO MONTHS SINCE SHE BECAME A POLICE WIDOW.

NICOLETTE KINNEAR:
My husband was a very firm person. He had a very stern persona. But I think I think it was because of this job. But he he had a heart of gold.

NICOLETTE KINNEAR:
He was a hands on kind of person. He what he did, he did with great passion. What he believed in what he started he would finish. And that is pretty much how he raised the boys as well. If you've committed to something and you've said yes to something, you've got to have to finish it.

VO:FOR THEIR SONS, CASLEIGH AND CARLISLE, TIME HAS NOT ERASED THE MEMORY OF THE AFTERNOON THEIR DAD DIED.

0:56 The clock was the last time that I spoke to my dad. So 1448. And then inside the clock, I have my Dad's force number. And then I got a rose. And my dad's favourite one of his favourite flowers was a Lily.


Piece to camera in Gearing Street, Bishop Lavis, site of murder
Charl Kinnear was a decorated police officer who worked on complex cases for the Anti-Gang Unit, a detective who worked on high risk dockets and got convictions. But he was shot in broad daylight, right here in Bishop Lavis outside his home in a car by a man in a hoodie who fled the scene.

(VO)
THIS BRAZEN ASSASSINATION ON THE 18TH OF SEPTEMBER 2020 SENT SHOCK WAVES THROUGH CAPE TOWN AND CHARL KINNEAR’S CLOSE COMMUNITY OF FELLOW POLICE OFFICERS.

Andre Lincoln
Former Head of the Anti-Gang Unit
I stood at the vehicle for a very long time, I just stood there and looked at his lifeless body and had this incredible anger running through me

Jeremy Vearey
Former Head of Detectives, Western Cape SAPS
These are people you build with, you have the been with them with through fire. And then you hand them over to other people, and they die….
They die because they were not looked after despite warnings and some evidence being there, that they are under threat, by parties up at national office, who have never seen the field.

NICOLETTE KINNEAR:
My husband was was shot five times. …And my boys still had the opportunity to kneel with him, with their dad and to pray with him, etc. By the time I came, It was chaos.

(VO)
NICOLETTE IS STILL CAMPAIGNING TO FIND ANSWERS. HIS COLLEAGUES KNEW HER HUSBAND WAS IN DANGER, THEY HAD BEEN ALERTED THAT HE WAS BEING MONITORED ILLEGALLY THROUGH HIS PHONE. BUT THE POLICE HAD NOT GIVEN HIM SPECIAL PROTECTION.

NICOLETTE KINNEAR
On the 16th - two days prior to his assassination. He also got a call from one of our senior ranking officers to tell him we are you your phone is being excessively pinged So that is why I say there's like a scenario we sitting in the parking area and we're just sitting and we were watching the bank being robbed and just doing nothing about.

(VO)
NICOLETTE BELIEVES SHE HAS NOW BEEN VINDICATED IN A REPORT BY THE INDEPENDENT POLICE INVESTIGATIVE DIRECTORATE - IPID - WHICH LAYS BARE THE FAULTLINES IN A FACTIONALISED POLICE FORCE TOO FRAGMENTED TO PROTECT THEIR OWN. IF THE POLICE HAD DONE THEIR JOB, SAYS THE REPORT, CHARL KINNEAR WOULD STILL BE ALIVE.

NICOLETTE KINNEAR (reading from the report)
“These members have dropped the proverbial ball and must therefore individually and collectively take responsible for the death of their colleague.”

(VO)
AT THE TIME OF HIS MURDER, CHARL KINNEAR WAS WORKING UNDER GENERAL ANDRE LINCOLN, WHO HEADED A UNIT TACKLING GANGS ON THE CAPE FLATS.
CARTE BLANCHE REPORTED ON HOW IT HAD BEEN SET UP WITH MUCH FANFARE IN 2018.
NOW RETIRED, ANDRE LIVES A SIMPLER LIFE, SUFFERING THE LOSS OF LIMBS DUE TO DIABETES.

ANDRE LINCOLN
We set out to bring peace and order to the the gang townships. It became it became so good at a point where just before COVID When we went into places like Hanover Park or Mitchell's Plan or Manenberg, people will say: Here come our people! Simply because I tried to bring over a new kind of policing.

(VO)
FOR GENERATIONS, CAPE FLATS COMMUNITIES HAVE BEEN UNDER SIEGE, ENSNARED IN DEADLY CRIMINAL GAMES OF GUNS, DRUGS AND EXTORTION.

Piece to Camera outside Cape Town High Court to intro Caryn Dolley
These courts have heard some of the most violent cases that have taken place as a result of the Cape’s Gang wars. Somebody with a front row seat and view of Cape Town's underworld is crime reporter Caryn Dolley.

CARYN DOLLEY
There's a common misconception that gangsterism in the Western Cape is limited to the Cape Flats. That's incorrect.I go so far as to say that gangs have stretched their tentacles into the corporate sector, into law enforcement, into policing.

(VO)
AS A COURT REPORTER CARYN DOLLEY HAS BEEN MAPPING THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN GANGS, CRIME BOSSES AND CORRUPT POLICE, FUELLED IN RECENT YEARS BY A FLOOD OF ILLEGAL FIREARMS TO THE CAPE.

CARYN DOLLEY
We've heard in court, how certain gangs control nightclub security, and that is not limited Cape flats, those are in city centres, sort of what we know as party strips, party hubs.

Piece to Camera in Long Street
Long street. It's a landmark strip popular amongst party goers in Cape Town. It's also turf for criminal syndicates, who demand payment from business owners here for protection.

JEREMY VEAREY
When somebody comes to you and forces down the service on you through intimidation, okay, to pay a certain fee for their services. Okay, that is what extortion is. And usually it involves Organised Crime rackets, , or gangs, that profiteer from that illegal act or forcing or intimidating you to take the service.

(VO)
FORMER MAJOR-GENERAL JEREMY VEAREY HEADED THE DETECTIVE SERVICES IN THE WESTERN CAPE BUT WAS FIRED LAST YEAR. HE WORKED CLOSELY WITH CHARL KINNEAR ON CASES THAT PRISED OPEN THE UNDERWORLD.

JEREMY VEAREY
Through every promotion that he had, I was on the panel. I placed him in units that gradually led to him investigating deeper organised crime in this province. So by the time that I handed him over to the gang unit, he was seasoned in the type of investigations of organised crime and gang related crime

(VO)
KINNEAR KNEW WHO CONTROLLED CAPE TOWN’S NIGHTLIFE. AND WHILE DELVING INTO CONNECTIONS BETWEEN GANGS AND CRIME BOSSES, ONE NAME KEPT CROPPING UP

ANDRE LINCOLN
Nafiz Modack was one of our prime targets. He was creating havoc in Cape Town whether it be individuals or business, or you were just all over the show. And we knew also that he was doing everything in his power to try and infiltrate and trying to infiltrate the entire game.

(VO)
NAFIZ MODACK IS NOW IN POLICE CUSTODY UNDER HEAVY GUARD, AWAITING TRIAL WITH A NUMBER OF CO-ACCUSED.

Pieces to Camera outside Cape Town High Court
Camera A Day #112
1:21 The trial against Nafiz Modack will be heard in September. He faces an astonishing number of charges - more than 3000 - including the murder of Charl Kinnear, other murders, attempted murders, extortion, dealing in illegal ammunition and firearms. And the list just goes on.

(VO)
BUT THIS MEGA-CASE IS ONLY ONE ELEMENT IN NICOLETTE’S STRUGGLE WHICH IS PITTING HER AGAINST SOME OF HER HUSBAND’S FORMER COLLEAGUES

NICOLETTE KINNEAR
35:20 We know my husband was investigating the underworld. And we also know my husband was investigating corruption within the police.

(VO)
IN 2018 CHARL KINNEAR SUBMITTED A DETAILED REPORT ALLEGING THAT A SO-CALLED ROGUE UNIT WAS OPERATING IN POLICE CRIMINAL INTELLIGENCE, SABOTAGING HIS WORK

CARYN DOLLEY
I think that Lieutenant Colonel Charl Kinnear's his 59 page letter of complaint shows that the state has blood on its hands. ……. And it's important to note that the crux of his complaint was that there were fellow police officers who were actively working against him and police officers perceived to be aligned to him. And what's more chilling, is that he said that these police officers were using state resources not to fight crime, but effectively stifle investigations him and his colleagues were busy with.

(VO)
CHARL’S COMPLAINT TRIGGERED A SERIES OF INTERNAL INVESTIGATIONS. IPID HAS NOW RECOMMENDED LAYING FORMAL CHARGES AGAINST POLICE OFFICERS. IT’S THERE ON PAPER - BUT NO TIMELINE OF ACTION.

Piece to camera outside Parliament
The iPid report into the murder of top detective Charl Kinnear was signed off on the 11th of May. It's meant to be tabled here in Parliament for a discussion, but no date has been set to interrogate the scathing report and the devastating findings of police failings.

NICOLETTE KINNEAR:
It’s this roller coaster that we're going around and around and ticking boxes, and ultimately, I feel wasting money and state resources.

(VO)
THE IPID REPORT SINGLES OUT ANDRE LINCOLN FOR SPECIAL CENSURE - AND RECOMMENDS THE CLOSURE OF THE ANTI-GANG UNIT.

ANDRE LINCOLN
Camera A Day Two # 112
27:37 Right from the beginning there was resistance from from the very top. It was a resistance from the former national commissioner to the formation of the Anti-Gang Unit. And they went out of their way to make sure that things didn't happen. .. So for Ipid to call for the the the disbanding of the Anti-Gang unit. I think they don't know what they're talking about.

From Andre Lincoln interview Camera A Day Two # 112
MASA 18:37 Do you feel the repercussions following what we've seen in the iPad report?

ANDRE LINCOLN
Andre Lincoln18:42 I don't think they can be any repercussions for me, not not criminally at least. Had I still been inside the police they probably could have charged me developmentally but criminally there's nothing that they can do to me because I didn't act in any way in any criminal way.

(VO)
BOTH ANDRE LINCOLN AND JEREMY VEAREY BLAME THE TOP BRASS OF THE SAPS, INCLUDING THE FORMER NATIONAL COMMISSIONER, KHEHLA SITOLE.

JEREMY VEAREY
Beside from departmental investigations and the criminal investigations against the rogue unit that is recommended by the iPid report, those civilians out there who were affected, like the Kinnear family should be given the information to empower them to hold these individuals civilly liable.

(VO)
POLICE MINISTER BHEKI CELE, THE SOUTH AFRICAN POLICE SERVICE AND IPID SAID THAT THE REPORT NEEDED FIRST TO BE DEALT WITH BY PARLIAMENT BEFORE THEY COULD COMMENT. THE FORMER POLICE COMMISSIONER, KEHLA SITHOLE, HAS ALSO DECLINED TO COMMENT.


(VO)
BACK HOME, THE WOUNDS ARE STILL RAW - NICOLETTE IS LAYING A BLANKET CHARGE OF CULPABLE HOMICIDE AGAINST ALL THOSE NAMED AND SHAMED IN THE IPID REPORT. HER SONS TAKE ISSUE WITH THEIR FATHER’S MENTORS, INCLUDING JEREMY VEAREY.

CARLISLE KINNEAR:
For years. he's been riding on my daddy's back,…my dad was a great detective, because he was a great detective. And for too long, it's been said that it's because of Veary that Kinnear climbed the ranks. It's not. If you look at my dad's track record as well, in 29 years of being a police officer, he lost one case.

(VO)
SAFETY IS NICOLETTE’S IMMEDIATE CONCERN, THIS WEEK SHE LEARNT SHE’S TO LOSE HALF HER POLICE PROTECTION. SHE IS NOT TAKING IT LYING DOWN.

NICOLETTE KINNEAR
I've come to see a side that that bleeds for for partners that left behind and needing to deal with trauma and still all of the admin and everything else that goes with it. It's really, really a steep, steep mountain to climb.

CARYN DOLLEY
I think she has picked up where her husband has left off in a sense she knows she can play a role in preventing this from happening to someone else



PROMOS


PROMO 1

VO: A cold-blooded assassination of a top cop investigating criminal networks – who is to blame for the death of Charl Kinnear? Crime bosses or the police they’ve compromised?

NICOLETTE KINNEAR
We know my husband was investigating the underworld. And we also know my husband was investigating corruption within the police.



PROMO 2

VO: Good cop and bad cop – an official report triggered by the assassination of decorated detective Charl Kinnear exposes deadly vendettas within our police

CARYN DOLLEY
What's more chilling, is that he said that these police officers were using state resources not to fight crime, but effectively stifle investigations him and his colleagues were busy with.


11 second promo
CARYN DOLLEY
I go so far as to say that gangs have stretched their tentacles into the corporate sector, into law enforcement, into policing.

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 10 August 2022 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Press Release: The Ultimate Price A thorn in the side of organised crime and a spear in the fight for justice, Lieutenant-Colonel Charl Kinnear was a highly decorated detective. His investigations disrupted the complex patterns of gang warfare and police complicity on the Cape Flats, in the Western Cape. It was a dangerous job at the best of times, and Kinnear should’ve enjoyed the support of his commanding officers, but according to an explosive new report, he was abandoned by his police bosses at the height of his investigations. Kinnear paid the ultimate price. After weeks of being tracked and followed by unknown assailants, the Lieutenant-Colonel was gunned down on his own doorstep. Now his wife, Nicolette, has stepped forward demanding justice for her husband’s senseless killing. Producer: Marion Edmunds | Presenter: Masa Kekana Script: (VO) WHATEVER THE WEATHER, NICOLETTE KINNEAR LAYS FLOWERS ON HER HUSBAND’S GRAVE WEEKLY. IT’S BECOME ROUTINE OVER THE TWENTY-TWO MONTHS SINCE SHE BECAME A POLICE WIDOW. NICOLETTE KINNEAR: My husband was a very firm person. He had a very stern persona. But I think I think it was because of this job. But he he had a heart of gold. NICOLETTE KINNEAR: He was a hands on kind of person. He what he did, he did with great passion. What he believed in what he started he would finish. And that is pretty much how he raised the boys as well. If you've committed to something and you've said yes to something, you've got to have to finish it. VO:FOR THEIR SONS, CASLEIGH AND CARLISLE, TIME HAS NOT ERASED THE MEMORY OF THE AFTERNOON THEIR DAD DIED. 0:56 The clock was the last time that I spoke to my dad. So 1448. And then inside the clock, I have my Dad's force number. And then I got a rose. And my dad's favourite one of his favourite flowers was a Lily. Piece to camera in Gearing Street, Bishop Lavis, site of murder Charl Kinnear was a decorated police officer who worked on complex cases for the Anti-Gang Unit, a detective who worked on high risk dockets and got convictions. But he was shot in broad daylight, right here in Bishop Lavis outside his home in a car by a man in a hoodie who fled the scene. (VO) THIS BRAZEN ASSASSINATION ON THE 18TH OF SEPTEMBER 2020 SENT SHOCK WAVES THROUGH CAPE TOWN AND CHARL KINNEAR’S CLOSE COMMUNITY OF FELLOW POLICE OFFICERS. Andre Lincoln Former Head of the Anti-Gang Unit I stood at the vehicle for a very long time, I just stood there and looked at his lifeless body and had this incredible anger running through me Jeremy Vearey Former Head of Detectives, Western Cape SAPS These are people you build with, you have the been with them with through fire. And then you hand them over to other people, and they die…. They die because they were not looked after despite warnings and some evidence being there, that they are under threat, by parties up at national office, who have never seen the field. NICOLETTE KINNEAR: My husband was was shot five times. …And my boys still had the opportunity to kneel with him, with their dad and to pray with him, etc. By the time I came, It was chaos. (VO) NICOLETTE IS STILL CAMPAIGNING TO FIND ANSWERS. HIS COLLEAGUES KNEW HER HUSBAND WAS IN DANGER, THEY HAD BEEN ALERTED THAT HE WAS BEING MONITORED ILLEGALLY THROUGH HIS PHONE. BUT THE POLICE HAD NOT GIVEN HIM SPECIAL PROTECTION. NICOLETTE KINNEAR On the 16th - two days prior to his assassination. He also got a call from one of our senior ranking officers to tell him we are you your phone is being excessively pinged So that is why I say there's like a scenario we sitting in the parking area and we're just sitting and we were watching the bank being robbed and just doing nothing about. (VO) NICOLETTE BELIEVES SHE HAS NOW BEEN VINDICATED IN A REPORT BY THE INDEPENDENT POLICE INVESTIGATIVE DIRECTORATE - IPID - WHICH LAYS BARE THE FAULTLINES IN A FACTIONALISED POLICE FORCE TOO FRAGMENTED TO PROTECT THEIR OWN. IF THE POLICE HAD DONE THEIR JOB, SAYS THE REPORT, CHARL KINNEAR WOULD STILL BE ALIVE. NICOLETTE KINNEAR (reading from the report) “These members have dropped the proverbial ball and must therefore individually and collectively take responsible for the death of their colleague.” (VO) AT THE TIME OF HIS MURDER, CHARL KINNEAR WAS WORKING UNDER GENERAL ANDRE LINCOLN, WHO HEADED A UNIT TACKLING GANGS ON THE CAPE FLATS. CARTE BLANCHE REPORTED ON HOW IT HAD BEEN SET UP WITH MUCH FANFARE IN 2018. NOW RETIRED, ANDRE LIVES A SIMPLER LIFE, SUFFERING THE LOSS OF LIMBS DUE TO DIABETES. ANDRE LINCOLN We set out to bring peace and order to the the gang townships. It became it became so good at a point where just before COVID When we went into places like Hanover Park or Mitchell's Plan or Manenberg, people will say: Here come our people! Simply because I tried to bring over a new kind of policing. (VO) FOR GENERATIONS, CAPE FLATS COMMUNITIES HAVE BEEN UNDER SIEGE, ENSNARED IN DEADLY CRIMINAL GAMES OF GUNS, DRUGS AND EXTORTION. Piece to Camera outside Cape Town High Court to intro Caryn Dolley These courts have heard some of the most violent cases that have taken place as a result of the Cape’s Gang wars. Somebody with a front row seat and view of Cape Town's underworld is crime reporter Caryn Dolley. CARYN DOLLEY There's a common misconception that gangsterism in the Western Cape is limited to the Cape Flats. That's incorrect.I go so far as to say that gangs have stretched their tentacles into the corporate sector, into law enforcement, into policing. (VO) AS A COURT REPORTER CARYN DOLLEY HAS BEEN MAPPING THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN GANGS, CRIME BOSSES AND CORRUPT POLICE, FUELLED IN RECENT YEARS BY A FLOOD OF ILLEGAL FIREARMS TO THE CAPE. CARYN DOLLEY We've heard in court, how certain gangs control nightclub security, and that is not limited Cape flats, those are in city centres, sort of what we know as party strips, party hubs. Piece to Camera in Long Street Long street. It's a landmark strip popular amongst party goers in Cape Town. It's also turf for criminal syndicates, who demand payment from business owners here for protection. JEREMY VEAREY When somebody comes to you and forces down the service on you through intimidation, okay, to pay a certain fee for their services. Okay, that is what extortion is. And usually it involves Organised Crime rackets, , or gangs, that profiteer from that illegal act or forcing or intimidating you to take the service. (VO) FORMER MAJOR-GENERAL JEREMY VEAREY HEADED THE DETECTIVE SERVICES IN THE WESTERN CAPE BUT WAS FIRED LAST YEAR. HE WORKED CLOSELY WITH CHARL KINNEAR ON CASES THAT PRISED OPEN THE UNDERWORLD. JEREMY VEAREY Through every promotion that he had, I was on the panel. I placed him in units that gradually led to him investigating deeper organised crime in this province. So by the time that I handed him over to the gang unit, he was seasoned in the type of investigations of organised crime and gang related crime (VO) KINNEAR KNEW WHO CONTROLLED CAPE TOWN’S NIGHTLIFE. AND WHILE DELVING INTO CONNECTIONS BETWEEN GANGS AND CRIME BOSSES, ONE NAME KEPT CROPPING UP ANDRE LINCOLN Nafiz Modack was one of our prime targets. He was creating havoc in Cape Town whether it be individuals or business, or you were just all over the show. And we knew also that he was doing everything in his power to try and infiltrate and trying to infiltrate the entire game. (VO) NAFIZ MODACK IS NOW IN POLICE CUSTODY UNDER HEAVY GUARD, AWAITING TRIAL WITH A NUMBER OF CO-ACCUSED. Pieces to Camera outside Cape Town High Court Camera A Day #112 1:21 The trial against Nafiz Modack will be heard in September. He faces an astonishing number of charges - more than 3000 - including the murder of Charl Kinnear, other murders, attempted murders, extortion, dealing in illegal ammunition and firearms. And the list just goes on. (VO) BUT THIS MEGA-CASE IS ONLY ONE ELEMENT IN NICOLETTE’S STRUGGLE WHICH IS PITTING HER AGAINST SOME OF HER HUSBAND’S FORMER COLLEAGUES NICOLETTE KINNEAR 35:20 We know my husband was investigating the underworld. And we also know my husband was investigating corruption within the police. (VO) IN 2018 CHARL KINNEAR SUBMITTED A DETAILED REPORT ALLEGING THAT A SO-CALLED ROGUE UNIT WAS OPERATING IN POLICE CRIMINAL INTELLIGENCE, SABOTAGING HIS WORK CARYN DOLLEY I think that Lieutenant Colonel Charl Kinnear's his 59 page letter of complaint shows that the state has blood on its hands. ……. And it's important to note that the crux of his complaint was that there were fellow police officers who were actively working against him and police officers perceived to be aligned to him. And what's more chilling, is that he said that these police officers were using state resources not to fight crime, but effectively stifle investigations him and his colleagues were busy with. (VO) CHARL’S COMPLAINT TRIGGERED A SERIES OF INTERNAL INVESTIGATIONS. IPID HAS NOW RECOMMENDED LAYING FORMAL CHARGES AGAINST POLICE OFFICERS. IT’S THERE ON PAPER - BUT NO TIMELINE OF ACTION. Piece to camera outside Parliament The iPid report into the murder of top detective Charl Kinnear was signed off on the 11th of May. It's meant to be tabled here in Parliament for a discussion, but no date has been set to interrogate the scathing report and the devastating findings of police failings. NICOLETTE KINNEAR: It’s this roller coaster that we're going around and around and ticking boxes, and ultimately, I feel wasting money and state resources. (VO) THE IPID REPORT SINGLES OUT ANDRE LINCOLN FOR SPECIAL CENSURE - AND RECOMMENDS THE CLOSURE OF THE ANTI-GANG UNIT. ANDRE LINCOLN Camera A Day Two # 112 27:37 Right from the beginning there was resistance from from the very top. It was a resistance from the former national commissioner to the formation of the Anti-Gang Unit. And they went out of their way to make sure that things didn't happen. .. So for Ipid to call for the the the disbanding of the Anti-Gang unit. I think they don't know what they're talking about. From Andre Lincoln interview Camera A Day Two # 112 MASA 18:37 Do you feel the repercussions following what we've seen in the iPad report? ANDRE LINCOLN Andre Lincoln18:42 I don't think they can be any repercussions for me, not not criminally at least. Had I still been inside the police they probably could have charged me developmentally but criminally there's nothing that they can do to me because I didn't act in any way in any criminal way. (VO) BOTH ANDRE LINCOLN AND JEREMY VEAREY BLAME THE TOP BRASS OF THE SAPS, INCLUDING THE FORMER NATIONAL COMMISSIONER, KHEHLA SITOLE. JEREMY VEAREY Beside from departmental investigations and the criminal investigations against the rogue unit that is recommended by the iPid report, those civilians out there who were affected, like the Kinnear family should be given the information to empower them to hold these individuals civilly liable. (VO) POLICE MINISTER BHEKI CELE, THE SOUTH AFRICAN POLICE SERVICE AND IPID SAID THAT THE REPORT NEEDED FIRST TO BE DEALT WITH BY PARLIAMENT BEFORE THEY COULD COMMENT. THE FORMER POLICE COMMISSIONER, KEHLA SITHOLE, HAS ALSO DECLINED TO COMMENT. (VO) BACK HOME, THE WOUNDS ARE STILL RAW - NICOLETTE IS LAYING A BLANKET CHARGE OF CULPABLE HOMICIDE AGAINST ALL THOSE NAMED AND SHAMED IN THE IPID REPORT. HER SONS TAKE ISSUE WITH THEIR FATHER’S MENTORS, INCLUDING JEREMY VEAREY. CARLISLE KINNEAR: For years. he's been riding on my daddy's back,…my dad was a great detective, because he was a great detective. And for too long, it's been said that it's because of Veary that Kinnear climbed the ranks. It's not. If you look at my dad's track record as well, in 29 years of being a police officer, he lost one case. (VO) SAFETY IS NICOLETTE’S IMMEDIATE CONCERN, THIS WEEK SHE LEARNT SHE’S TO LOSE HALF HER POLICE PROTECTION. SHE IS NOT TAKING IT LYING DOWN. NICOLETTE KINNEAR I've come to see a side that that bleeds for for partners that left behind and needing to deal with trauma and still all of the admin and everything else that goes with it. It's really, really a steep, steep mountain to climb. CARYN DOLLEY I think she has picked up where her husband has left off in a sense she knows she can play a role in preventing this from happening to someone else PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: A cold-blooded assassination of a top cop investigating criminal networks – who is to blame for the death of Charl Kinnear? metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We meet a police widow fighting for justice after her husband’s murder
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Nicolette Kinnear lost her husband in a cold-blooded assassination in broad daylight on their doorstep, in gang-ridden Bishop Lavis in Cape Town. Lieutenant-Colonel Charl Kinnear was an experienced and award-winning detective who through his investigations disrupted the complex patterns of gang warfare, criminality and police complicity which mark the Cape Flats out as a ganglands. Kinnear’s murder was linked by the police to the crime empire of Nafiz Modack and one of his henchmen, Zane Killian, who had been illegally tracking Kinnear’s movements – apparently 2116 times through cellphone triangulation, depicting his exact movements. At the time of the murder, Kinnear was investigating a gun-running case which implicated Modack and 8 senior policemen. However, there is also speculation that the murder could have been a commissioned gang hit, because of his Kinnear’s success at convicting two 28 members that week. What is clear is that the ongoing vendettas between power blocs within the Western Cape Police Service, and the lack of support Kinnear received from his employer, the SAPS, left the capable and competent detective extremely vulnerable, all the more so after he had fingered officials and exposed faultlines in a whistle-blower’s report two years earlier. Since Kinnear’s death on the 18 September 2020, Nicolette and her two sons have been waiting for justice to be done – and when she got sight of the final IPID report into her husband’s death wanted to speak out about how he and her family have been failed.
metadata.Summary: The court case of Nafiz Modack loaded with extortion charges will take place in September and will include the Charl Kinnear assassination and as well as the attempted murder of Advocate William Booth on 9 April 2020, among many other charges. There will be about 28 accused. Modack is alleged to have funded these particular hits as well as others. This mega-trial will lay bare the story of the “Nafiz Modack Enterprise” which among other things channelled cash to hitmen through his business Empire Investment Cars. As the state lays down the full evidence, so will emerge a portrait of Modack as a violent criminal on the make, heavily involved in racketeering and extortion, with blood on his hands. Nicolette has been cold-shouldered by the bosses of her husband – former top cops Jeremy Veary and Peter Jacobs, who have made no attempt to reach out to her in this time of desolation. However, she did receive a letter concealed in a bunch of flower son her husband’s grave which drew a picture of a roundtable discussion involving gang members and police officials which determined her husband’s death. These point the finger at Ralph Stanfield, leader of the 28’s who “own” Bishop Lavis and Valhalla Park. This allegation has not been proved in any way.
metadata.Further information: The convictions secured by Charl Kinnear in the week of his murder were for two 28 gangsters, Ashwin Willemse alias ‘Krag” and Waylin Abdulla alias “Wena” who were found guilty on two counts of murder, aggravated robbery and possession of firearms and ammunition. Their victims were Gregory “Kallie” Carelse who sustained 16 shots to his body, and Prezano Holland on 18 October 2018. Carelse, a local hero in the community, was close to Kinnear as he was a former police reservist. Carelse himself had been involved in arresting members of the Stanfield clan a year earlier, and witness to a drive-by shooting which claimed three lives. Another policeman Colonel Andre Kay who lived a few doors down from the Kinnears was also hit on 14 Nov 2019 outside his residence. His body, pumped with ten bullets, was found by his 81-year old mother in the driveway. He was attached to the Fire Arms, Liquor and Second hand goods Control unit, loved his job, lived with his mother and was universally liked. Nicolette wants to speak out because she feels the state is failing her family, failed her husband while he was working as an organized crime investigator, and fails other families in her position. Given the rate of murder of community leaders, lawyers and policemen in the Western Cape, her story has relevance. She takes a deep interest in the trial of Modack, and receives a great deal of inside information from all over, including police reports before they have been tabled. However she is anxious about her safety and her future. The most recent IPID report, which left her reeling, ought to be tabled in Parliament by controversial ANC politician, Tina Joemat-Pettersen, chair of the police portfolio committee, but there is no clarity when and whether MPs will be using it to hold the failed police service to account. Many of the people fingered in the IPID report have already left the service, without experiencing any penalties, despite their complicity or neglect. Others who were fingered remain in place in SAPS.
